column1: # nihilurk's compatibility matrix: one row per machine nihilurk claims to run on.
# This file is the pipeline. `cross_build.sh` builds a row and `run_check.sh`
# checks that the row's image has a shell and that the binary actually starts
# there; the report prints a row per row. Adding a machine is adding a line
# here; nothing else knows the list. (Same rule as the content tables -- see
# docs/explanation/adr-0001-tables-not-raws.md.)
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   id        short name, used for file names and report rows
#   target    rust target triple
#   class     linux  -- has an OS, a terminal and a shell; nihilurk runs here
#             bare   -- no OS; only `particle-core` is built, and only checked
#   platform  docker --platform value for a `native` row, or "-" for bare
#             metal. A `qemu` row's container runs as the host's own
#             architecture instead (see run_check.sh), so this column only
#             tells it which static interpreter to fetch.
#   image     runtime image the binary is executed in, or the SDK image for bare
#   exec      native -- the host CPU runs it directly
#             qemu   -- run under a directly-invoked qemu-user-static
#                        interpreter; needs no binfmt_misc and no --privileged
#             none   -- not executed at all (bare metal)
#   note      what real machine this row is standing in for
# House rule: every `linux` row's image must have a shell in it (alpine's
# /bin/sh, in every row here). That is not decoration -- nihilurk needs a real
# terminal to draw into, and a distroless or scratch image can't give it one,
# so a row without a shell couldn't run the game if it wanted to. `linux`
# rows other than the two natives (`cloud`, `potato`) are all ARM boards
# people actually run a full Linux + shell on -- Pi 2 through 4 and the
# Compute Module -- rather than instances that only exist as cloud abstractions,
# because the point of this matrix is "does nihilurk run on that hardware", and a
# board is hardware in a way a VM SKU is not. `graviton` is kept anyway: an
# M-series Mac's Linux VM is a real, common way nihilurk gets built and played.
# `run_check.sh` checks the shell claim before it trusts it -- see
# `check_has_shell` in lib.sh.
# There is no CPU or memory cap here, and there used to be one. nihilurk has no
# workload that asks a machine to be fast: every feel-layer effect is bounded,
# so the actual claim this matrix makes is narrower and cheaper to check --
# if it builds, the image has a shell, and the target is std (every `linux`
# row here is), nihilurk can run there. See
# docs/explanation/cross-platform-testing.md.
#id
cloud
column7: t3.micro / any x86_64 box, and the control: no emulation

column1: graviton
column7: AWS Graviton (t4g.nano), an M-series Mac's Linux VM

column1: pi-zero
column7: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, Pi 1/2 class hardware
